result.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Internal Computation for Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Iterative neural policies usually spend the same computation on every decision, although the benefit of additional processing varies across states. We introduce Adaptive Internal Computation (AIC), an iterative policy that learns when to stop refining its latent representation and act. In AIC, we train action selection and stopping jointly, an expected-depth penalty values computation and intermediate value predictions provide auxiliary supervision. We show that when only some states benefit from further refinement, an ideal state-dependent allocator outperforms every state-independent stopping schedule at the same expected depth. With at most eight refinement steps per decision, AIC executes 3.3 steps on average across twelve benchmark tasks and lowers per-decision latency by 31--44% relative to a fixed eight-step policy on four control and robotics tasks. Its mean reward exceeds the best fixed-depth policy on seven tasks and trails it on four. Ablating adaptive stopping and value supervision separately shows that stopping accounts for most of the reward gain on PickCube and AntMaze, where it also executes more refinement steps and that supervision accounts for most of it on RareEvent.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Adaptive Internal Computation（AIC）：一种迭代策略，联合训练动作选择与「何时停止精炼 latent 表示」，并以期望深度惩罚与中间价值预测作为辅助监督；在十二个基准上平均 3.3 步，相较固定八步策略降低 31–44% 单决策延迟，奖励在七个任务上优于最佳固定深度策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯 RL 控制任务，但其状态自适应的停止学习、深度惩罚与中间价值监督可能直接对应 LVR 中 STOP 决策与动态计算分配的收益-成本问题，可供核查能否迁移到 VLM 推理期的停止判据与监督设计。
